This is the most efficient method I've found. If anyone could make it even more so, I'm open to suggestions. However, this method has worked for me.

This will require some initial work up front in photoshop/GIMP, but even if you're a novice at this (like me) you can do it.

  1. Get some images. I would recommend vector files, but .png files will work too, jpegs meh but ok. The higher resolution the better. Ideally you want them without a background so they don't have a white box around them in night mode. If not that's fine, you can remove it in photoshop. Once you have your images how you want them to appear, you're going to want to resize them so they're all the same. Again this can be done in photoshop. I would recommend somewhere around 30px width X 20pix height, 25x25, or 20x20. Go ahead and create a blank transparent image the same size as your others, this will be the "default flair" for anyone that doesn't want an image flair.

  2. Take your new image flairs and find an online sprite sheet generator. I've used retinaspritegenerator.com but others will probably work too. Upoload your images. This is important, make sure your "default flair", the blank one, is first in the list. Choose your orientation of your spritesheet. I've found vertical is easiest on the css. And click generate sprite and css. Save the sprite sheet and upload it to an image host and hang on to the image url.

  3. Open your css file in notepad++ or whatever text editor you use. You need to change quite a few things. So starting from the top, you'll see the .sprite element. This is where you'll specify that this sprite sheet applies to all users. replace .sprite with #container a[href^="/user/"]::after. Now you need to specify the properties. The following are the properties I've used and it works for me. 

#container a[href^="/user/"]::after {
 display: inline-block; 
 content: ""; 
 background-repeat: no-repeat;
 background-position: left top;
 padding: 0px; 
 margin: 0px; 
 margin-left: 5px;
 background-color: transparent; 
 background-image: url("YourSpriteSheetUrl.com"); 
 width: 30px; 
 height: 20px;
 vertical-align: middle;
}

You'll want to change the background-image url and the width and height properties to match your individual flair images. Moving down the css, you'll see the background-image property again change the url. Below that you'll see .sprite-image1 and so on. Comment these out as they're just the names of your individual images, you can rename them to make things easier. Under each individual flair you'll see the width, height, and background-position properties. Delete the width and height.

Now after the commented out flair names, but before the individual properties is where you'll define the flair for each individual user. To do that use this #container a[href="/user/user1"]::after. If you are assigning multiple users to the same image, you'll just separate them by a comma. Make sure the last one before the properties is not followed by a comma. So it will look like this:

/* dickbutt */ 
#container a[href="/user/user1"]::after,
#container a[href="/user/user2"]::after,
#container a[href="/user/user3"]::after {
 background-position: 0 -20px;
}

Do this for however many flairs and users you have. If someone doesn't want a flair they will get the "default blank flair" automatically. You shouldn't have to mess with the background-position properties, so you can leave those as they are.

Note: when assigning users, usernames are case sensitive. So keep that in mind when you see a lowercase "L" but it's really an uppercase "i" or vice versa.

This method will override any other user flairs such as text flair.

Prior to becoming a mod, I didn't know any css and this was my first "big" project. So if any of you css masters want to critique or help me improve, your feedback is appreciated.

Edit: fixed error pointed out by @j_

A minor point: use ^= for the shared styles, but = for the specific selectors, i.e.:

#container a[href^="/user/"]::after {
 display: inline-block; 
 …
}

#container a[href="/user/user1"]::after {
 background-position: 0 -20px;
}

If you use ^= for user1, it can match user1a, user123 etc.

You can read more about attribute selectors here.
